name: Chin wing osteotomy

lead: A chin wing osteotomy is an oral and maxillofacial surgery technique that extends a sliding genioplasty back along the lower border of the jaw. The cut bone is repositioned and the gaps are typically filled with bone graft, which can advance and lengthen the chin and add width and definition toward the jaw angle.

Surgeons describe it for retrognathic chins, jaw asymmetry and lower-face contour, sometimes together with orthognathic surgery. Published evidence consists mainly of technical notes and small case series.

paras: It is done by a surgeon under general anaesthesia, often planned with digital imaging and sometimes with custom cutting guides and plates. Some patients compare it with custom jaw-angle implants, a choice discussed at length on looksmaxxing forums.

A 2026 study notes the main concern is inferior alveolar nerve damage, which makes the procedure less used than classic genioplasty. Forum users report dissatisfaction, contour problems and revisions in some cases. Surgeon experience matters.

lead: Chin wing osteotomy is an extended form of genioplasty in which the bone cut runs from the chin region along the body of the mandible toward the jaw angle, so that the lower border of the jaw can be moved forward, lengthened or reshaped as a single unit. The technique is most often credited to the Italian surgeon Albino Triaca and is sometimes called Triaca's chin wing or wing genioplasty. [1][2][3]

For someone who wants a better-looking lower face, the appeal is that one operation can do several things at once: project a recessed chin, lengthen a short lower third, and add width and definition along the jawline toward the gonial angle, using the person's own bone rather than an implant. Case reports describe it for retrognathic patients whose bite is already normal, so the teeth do not need to be repositioned. [4][5]

The published literature consists mainly of technical notes, single case reports and small retrospective series, including a 2026 study of 26 patients that examined the inferior alveolar nerve concerns that have limited the technique's use. On looksmax.org it is discussed as 'genioplasty on steroids', compared with custom jaw-angle implants and with bimaxillary surgery, and users post both enthusiastic and regretful accounts. [6][7][8]

paras: A standard sliding genioplasty cuts a horseshoe-shaped piece from the front of the lower jaw and slides it forward, backward or vertically before fixing it with plates. [9] The chin wing extends that cut posteriorly along the horizontal part of the mandible, so a longer segment of the lower border moves with the chin. Surgeons describe this as allowing the chin prominence, the angle of divergence of the lower border and lip position to be adjusted independently of the dental bases, which matters when the bite does not need to change. [8][2]

The space created behind the advanced segment is typically filled with bone graft or other material, and the segment is held with plates and screws. A 2013 short communication described a modification of Triaca's osteotomy to vertically correct the lower border in a patient with horizontal-growth condylar hyperplasia and facial asymmetry. [3]

A mini wing variant, described in 2020, ends the posterior cut at the upper part of the mandibular notch and spares the basilar edge of the jaw. Its authors report that it can be combined with bilateral sagittal split osteotomy (BSSO) for dento-skeletal deformity and that, unlike the traditional wing, a very low inferior alveolar nerve is not a contraindication. [10]

A 2021 technical note described custom cutting guides and implants intended to make the procedure safer and quicker, and a 2021 case report combined a chin wing with a 'pyramid' of layered cortical bone graft from the ramus and custom malar implants in a 40-year-old man who wanted greater chin projection and more prominent mandibular angles. [11][12]

Triaca's chin wing mentoplasty is cited in later papers as the origin of the technique. [1][3] A 2014 abstract in Head & Face Medicine titled 'Chin wing osteotomy - a new facial concept' presented it as a facial concept rather than only a deformity correction. [2] Papers in 2013 and 2015 reported modifications for condylar hyperplasia, hyper-divergent skeletal class III deformity and bilateral Goldenhar syndrome, in which the wing replaced or supplemented bimaxillary surgery. [3][1][13]

A 2018 paper on the lower facial third noted that techniques such as V-line surgery and the chin wing had risen in popularity to change the frontal and lateral shape of the lower third, and that no reference standard existed for how far such changes should go. In that study, 202 raters scored photographs of 24 female models, pairing ratings with the gonial-to-chin angle measured in frontal view. [5]

Genioplasty in general is performed for profile and facial balance. [9] Reported uses of the wing variant include asymmetric mandibles such as Goldenhar syndrome and condylar hyperplasia, hyperdivergent skeletal class III deformity, and cosmetic contouring in patients with normal occlusion and a retrognathic mandible. [1][3][13][4]

Forum users describe goals in terms of the frontal view: a narrow lower third, a short chin or lack of width at the jaw angle that they feel a bimax would not change. One poster describing the dilemma said he ruled out facial implants because he did not want foreign bodies in his face for life. [7] Others compare it with custom jaw-angle implants, with the main trade-off framed as autologous bone and chin projection versus a simpler implant operation. [14]

In general terms it is an intraoral operation under general anaesthesia performed by an oral and maxillofacial or craniofacial surgeon. Planning is often digital: a 2022 case report describes cone beam CT, Dolphin Imaging simulation and CAD-designed cutting and repositioning guides, with L-shaped plates and bone grafts at the mandibular angle. [4] Surgeons may stage it after BSSO in patients who had orthognathic surgery first. [6]
Recovery follows jaw surgery norms: swelling, a soft diet and temporary lip numbness are common after genioplasty procedures, and surgeon experience is described as helping reduce complications. [9]

The inferior alveolar nerve runs through the segment of bone the wing cut passes near, and the 2026 Journal of Stomatology, Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery paper states that the chin wing is little used mainly because of the greater risk of nerve damage than classic genioplasty. Its retrospective series of 26 patients who had BSSO first and then a chin wing analysed the rate of nerve damage and its impact on daily life. [6]

Genioplasty as a family carries risks of swelling, hematoma, temporary lip weakness or numbness, infection, bone changes and nerve injury. [9] Forum posters report outcomes they consider unsatisfactory, such as persistent recession, contour irregularities at the gonial angle and revision surgery, in threads with titles such as 'still recessed after chin wing' and 'surgery i need to fix chin wing mess'. [15][16]

On looksmax.org, chin wing sits in the tier of facial-bone surgeries discussed alongside sliding genioplasty, custom jaw-angle implants, bimax and the surgeons associated with them. A widely read thread presents it as a 'very powerful, yet under-looked' operation and quotes the technique's own paper to explain it, then summarises it as the lower jaw being sliced, moved forward and grafted. [8] Other threads weigh it against custom implants, discuss mini wing versus full wing for lengthening the lower third, share individual experiences, and compare surgeon-and-implant combinations. [14][17][18]

Cost, surgeon choice and unpredictability of the result are recurring themes, as in a thread asking what it costs in different regions. [19] Posts range from users who like the result to users who report regret; one thread reply describes another member as regretting his chin wing. [7]

Published human reports are technical notes, case reports and small series. They include two retrognathic patients with normal occlusion followed for four years after guide-assisted chin wing surgery, who reported favourable aesthetic and functional results and chin advancement with improved contour. [4] A Goldenhar syndrome case reported aesthetic, functional and histological considerations. [1] The 26-patient 2026 series examined nerve outcomes after chin wing in patients who had already had BSSO. [6] No randomised trial comparing chin wing with implants or sliding genioplasty is described in these papers.
